title: Rich Dark Hot Chocolate (Chocolat Chaud)
dish_title: Hot chocolate (French chocolat chaud, Spanish thick)
summary: Cocoa is whisked into boiling water, then whole milk; chopped dark chocolate, sugar and a pinch of salt are melted in until glossy and slightly thick, and vanilla goes in at the end.

ingredients.note: about 1 tbsp; up to 3 tbsp to taste

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Bloom the cocoa
steps.text: Bring the water to the boil in the saucepan, then whisk in the cocoa to a smooth paste; a few lumps are fine. Hot water releases the cocoa's flavour.

steps.title: Add the milk
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium and whisk in the milk, sweeping around the sides of the pan to dissolve the cocoa.

steps.title: Melt the chocolate
steps.text: When the milk starts to steam and bubble at the edges, whisk in the chocolate, 1 tbsp sugar and the salt. Turn the heat to low and whisk for 2-3 minutes until melted, glossy and slightly thickened; don't let it boil hard.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Taste and whisk in more sugar if you like, then take the pan off the heat and whisk in the vanilla.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour into the mugs and serve straight away; it thickens further as it cools.

tips: Chop the chocolate finely so it melts evenly without scorching.
Dutch-processed cocoa is darker and smoother; natural cocoa works but is tangier.
Serve it in small mugs: it is rich enough to be a dessert.
For a thinner drink, whisk in an extra 100 ml hot milk.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers, covered, for up to 2 days. Reheat gently, whisking. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
